description: Repo-scoped GitHub pull-request tools for engineering agents: read a PR, assess its deterministic risk level, propose a targeted-edit fix, and review (COMMENT or risk-gated APPROVE under a second identity). Registers a resource and ships a stdio MCP server.

outputs.description: GithubPrTools toolset, callable in-process or served over stdio MCP

resource_key.label: Resource Key
resource_key.description: Resource key the toolset is registered under.

repo.label: Repo
repo.description: GitHub repository the tools are scoped to, 'owner/repo'. Every call is pinned to this repo.

token_env_var.label: Token Env Var
token_env_var.description: Env var holding the primary GitHub token (reads, COMMENT reviews, propose_fix, merge).

reviewer_token_env_var.label: Reviewer Token Env Var
reviewer_token_env_var.description: Env var holding a SECOND GitHub token (a distinct bot/user identity with write access) -- required for an APPROVE review. GitHub blocks a PR's own author (or a single bot identity that opened it) from approving it, so APPROVE always needs a genuinely different identity's token.

api_base_url.label: Api Base Url
api_base_url.description: API base URL. Change for GitHub Enterprise Server.

base_branch.label: Base Branch
base_branch.description: Base branch for propose_fix's pull requests.

branch_prefix.label: Branch Prefix
branch_prefix.description: Prefix propose_fix uses for the branches it creates.

protected_paths.label: Protected Paths
protected_paths.description: Path prefixes propose_fix refuses to touch (CI, dependencies, packaging).

low_risk_paths.label: Low Risk Paths
low_risk_paths.description: Path prefixes assess_pull_request/review_pull_request treat as low-risk when nothing else disqualifies the PR.

low_risk_max_files.label: Low Risk Max Files
low_risk_max_files.description: assess_pull_request: max changed files for a 'low' risk level.

low_risk_max_lines.label: Low Risk Max Lines
low_risk_max_lines.description: assess_pull_request: max changed lines (additions + deletions) for a 'low' risk level.

max_files_per_fix.label: Max Files Per Fix
max_files_per_fix.description: propose_fix: max files a single fix may change.

allow.label: Allow
allow.description: Hard allow-list of tools (default: all). Valid: get_pull_request, list_open_pull_requests, assess_pull_request, propose_fix, review_pull_request.

max_result_chars.label: Max Result Chars
max_result_chars.description: Upper bound on the serialized size of any tool result.

mcp_server_resource_key.label: Mcp Server Resource Key
mcp_server_resource_key.description: If set, ALSO registers a stdio MCP-server-shaped resource under this key (python -m this module, with GITHUB_PR_TOOLS_* env vars set from this component's own settings, and the real token(s) passed through via live env passthrough). Any mcp_servers-aware component can then reference it via server_resource_key.

mcp_extra_env_vars.label: Mcp Extra Env Vars
mcp_extra_env_vars.description: mcp_server_resource_key only. Extra env var NAMES (beyond the token env vars, which are always passed through) to copy into the spawned MCP server's env.

practice_mode_env_var.label: Practice Mode Env Var
practice_mode_env_var.description: Env var NAME (not a value templated into this field) whose value, read fresh at call time, switches propose_fix into practice mode: every validation (protected paths, duplicate-PR-file check, file count) still runs, but no branch/commit/PR is actually created -- {'practice_mode': True, 'would_open': 'pull_request', ...} is returned instead. Same vocabulary as the engineering-agents reference's settings.shadow(): any value except '', '0', 'false', 'no', 'off' (case-insensitive) is ON. Scope this to a Dagster+ branch deployment (set the env var there, leave it unset in the full deployment) to practice in a PR's own branch deployment and act for real after merge.

ledger_path.label: Ledger Path
ledger_path.description: Directory this tool writes one JSON-lines file per Dagster run_id into, recording every consequential action (propose_fix, open_issue, an APPROVE review) as it happens -- filed, would_file (practice mode), refused (a guardrail declined it), or decision_needed (e.g. an 'Kind: improvement' PR an APPROVE rule always refers to a person). The run_id comes from MCP's out-of-band request _meta (see each agent component's own run_id threading), NOT a tool argument -- a prompt cannot spoof which run an entry belongs to. Point an agent component's own outcome_ledger_path at this SAME directory to read it back. Unset: no ledger is written (zero behavior change).

restrict_to_branch_prefix.label: Restrict To Branch Prefix
restrict_to_branch_prefix.description: When true, get_pull_request/list_open_pull_requests/assess_pull_request/review_pull_request all refuse (GithubPrScopeError) to operate on a PR whose head branch doesn't start with branch_prefix -- never a human's or a bot's (e.g. dependabot's) PR. Off by default, since this toolset also works as a general-purpose PR reviewer for any PR. Turn this on when pairing with sensors/github_pull_request_agent_sensor (which already only ever launches runs for branch_prefix PRs) -- a second layer of defense covering a manually-invoked chat agent or a hallucinated PR number.

exclude_paths.label: Exclude Paths
exclude_paths.description: Path prefixes the agent may neither READ nor change -- get_pull_request/assess_pull_request/review_pull_request never include a matching file in the PR's file list at all (not just refuse to approve touching it), propose_fix refuses to change one, list_files never includes a matching entry in its listing at all, and read_file refuses to read one. For when the repository that hosts these agent components is the SAME repository they review (e.g. 'assets/ai/github_pr_tools/' for this repo's own copy) -- without this, a review agent spends its review on its own source instead of the PR it's actually meant to look at. Same directory-like/filename-like matching convention as protected_paths.

duplicate_check_lookback_days.label: Duplicate Check Lookback Days
duplicate_check_lookback_days.description: find_issues includes an issue closed within this many days, not just still-open ones. A person closing a bad finding (wontfix, already handled) is a signal not to re-file it -- without this, that signal is lost the moment the issue drops out of an open-only search, and an advisor agent re-files the same thing it was already told no about.

validate_python_snippets.label: Validate Python Snippets
validate_python_snippets.description: open_issue parses every Python/diff code block in the body and refuses to file (with the specific reason) if a Dagster import, attribute, or call doesn't match the INSTALLED dagster -- e.g. a renamed/removed function, or a call whose arguments don't match the real signature. Catches a wrong suggestion before it's filed, not after a person tries it and it fails. Best-effort: a snippet that doesn't parse as Python at all is checked line by line instead of being skipped.
